RuneType.Description: My first hammer, given to me by my mother when I was but a boy. Bested many a foe with it before I cracked it on the nose of a stone giant.
Not my own sword, mind you. Belonged to the foul King Ulther. He claimed it was magic and that made him king. I snapped the blade off and beat him senseless with the handle.
Was a time when the sound of this war horn set my foes shivering with fear. That time continues unto this very day, although now you might see a god or two shiver as well.
I never was one for magic and spells and such dark mysteries. But I took this Runestone from a mother troll’s den. It brought me luck almost to the day I died.
All I ever knew of my father. They said he was the fiercest bear ever that ever lived.
It was wolf or me when I was only three. Last time a wolf was that foolish in my presence.
The terror of my home fjords, it would chew whole longships to splinters if it smelled cod on board. I learned to swim chasing this toothy, great fish.
My first famous deed. This monster had been eating its fill every night in the Jarl’s feast hall. No weapon could scratch it, so I took that arm off with my bare hands.
A sneak of a snake. Hid in wells and came out at night. I thought the poison was in its tongue. Found out the hard way that’s not true.
This bullying brute’s bellowing caused an avalanche when I hit him the first time. Now he’s nice and quiet.
My trip across the Western Sea got cut short when this beast grappled my longship. I had to sail its carcass back home.
My last act on Earth, but at least I took this flame-spoutings sack of scales with me. I hear tell he found his own heaven with the Fire Giants.
My proudest day was in Paris (the one in Texas, not Pah-ree, France) when I was commissioned Deputy U.S. Marshal.
I don’t set much by luck and whatnot, but this old shoe brought more worries than a herd of preachers. I took to sneakin’ it into the saddlebags of those as gave me cause for worry.
Cast this .45 round my ownself as a present for a fellow Marshal. But one thing led to another, and I was in desperate need of a bullet to save President Grant from certain undead desperadoes.
This battered old war bonnet looks moth eaten, but those holes come from Max Burr’s scattergun. Left it atop a scarecrow while I got the jump on the rascal from the tall grass.
This bumpkin made off with thirty head of cattle from my uncle’s ranch and tried rebranding ‘em. I tracked him thirty miles east and hogtied him for the sheriff. Not bad for a girl of thirteen.
Sadie Hooks and her Trout Teeth Gang would hide in ponds, waiting to ambush helpless travelers. How I cottoned to fishin’ with dynamite.
The Clockwork Count of Dodge City and his automatons busted into every bank of note between the Rockies and the Mississippi. I had to used magnetic bullets just to hit his clockwork safe-crackers.
I caught this devilish deviant grave robbing outside Eldorado Canyon, Nevada. That night his zombies busted him out of the hoosegow, and I spent three sleepless nights resting them all in pieces.
This bovine bandita was not so much rustlin’ cattle as “liberating them.” We came to an understanding after one heckuva tussle, and she took her gang on up to Wisconsin.

Caught this curious fella runnin’ a faro game in Ruby, Arizona. I took hold of him, but there weren’t nothin’ under those bandages he wore! Followed his footprints for three weeks before wrangling him.
This self-proclaimed Emperor of New Texas was rasing an army of desperadoes. I snuck into one of his secret fandangos and got the drop on him. Weren’t near so tough caught with his trousers down.

Famous for the Greatest Train Robbery out in San Fran, Zhao Shih stole an entire Western Pacific train and sold all 18 rail cars in Manilla. I caught up to her outside of Tombstone, and we had more than words.
Shouting, “Griffin Knights, Unite!” I’d activate my homing beacon to summon my Warbot. Loved the shocked look on Oort Trooper faces when my ‘bot flew over the horizon, roaring like a monster.
As Knight Prime, I headed of the entire Warbot formation. Whether we were fighting toe to toe on the ground or piloting our Griffs in space, this headset united me with my fellow knights.
The Oort Empire came not from another star but from another dimension. The reality-bending O.M.T. was the only way to strike back against the Oort Lich King and save Earth.

Cloned from the essences of Earth’s greatest heroes, the heroic destiny of The Knights Stellar was literally in our genes. This bearlike ole’ bruiser was the basis for my hard-hitting DNA, and his bobblehead sat proudly in my Griff’s cockpit.
Oort Troopers hide behind particle shields and lasguns. Cy-Jitsu trained us to charge in and deliver the finishing blow point blank, whether we’re wielding Vibro Spears or piloting battle Griffs.
My mentor and wingman, Taurus the Green Knight, fell during the Solstice Offence of 2368. He was leading our team through the Lunar trenches when the Oorts ambushed us.

SynthStar Ako Lennon von Mozart generated this stirring anthem as a tribute to my victory on the Lunar Front, it topped every Earthling’s playlists for the rest of the war. I especially love the whalesong chorus.
When the Oort Empire Gargantunauts warped into orbit, studded with fiery plasma claws and gnashing planet-crusher jaws, everyone thought Earth was doomed. Everyone but me and my fellow knights.
Picked from the ruins of the Mars Colony hydroponics dome, this lucky piece of green gave me hope on one of my bleakest days. Plus it glows green when you sing to it.
Stuck in the ground, the spike poisons whole planets with Oort anti-life particles. I had to kick, stab, and spear my way past a thousand troopers to yank it from the Martian soil in time.

The Griffin Warbot’s Emblazoned Blade was our secret weapon. We could only activate it for a few seconds at a time, since the edge was hotter than the surface of the sun. I seldom needed more than a full second.
Never delivered. Always preferred the Red Knight. I guess marriage and all that would’ve been too distracting, right? Seriously though, I wish them all the best.
I was the first to claim the rank of Star Marshal in 712 cycles. All the Selenite loyalists rallied to my cause, knowing that under my command alone could the Martians be defeated.
This little fellow has been with me since I was but a spawnling. I find his overly-large eyes and diminutive frame to be quite charming.
I created the Eon Throne as a fitting seat of power for my new empire. Hewn from the heart of a dwarf star, any other who sits upon it would be instantly crushed.
Only I, Lord Vraxx the Conqueror, know what will happen should I choose to press this button. Of course I know. I know exactly what it will do. Exactly. No doubt at all.
A grand craft, the pride of our space force. All would tremble to hear its fearsome hum and none was more skilled a pilot than the youthful ace, Vraxx.
I toppled thirty Tripods during the First Martian War. If one knows the secret, it’s simply a matter of superb skill to reflect their own heat rays back upon them.
The Oort Imperium’s answer to our gorgeous saucers. I single-handedly saved the Selenite Armada when I proved these fighters’ tremendous speed was of no use in Saturn’s Rings.
Invulnerable to all known weaponry, it took a leader of my unprecedented genius to realize their one weakness was their general’s insufferable pride.
Others feared these monstrous entities. I discovered how to communicate with them. Their secrets helped me do what the Starslime could not: seize the Selenite Throne.
Now that I was Lord Vraxx, I could lead our people to glory. The Venusians offered fierce resistance, but my skilled soldiers outfought them at every turn.
Of course this so-called peace envoy was a spy for the Martian resistance. Many doubted my decision, but doubters and Interdimensional spies both paid the ultimate price for defying me.
This being’s strange riddles and trans-temporal missile system almost defeated my intellect. Almost, of course. Even a mighty toad is no match for Lord Vraxx!
Fight darkness. Fight cold. Fight hunger. Fire fights for The Clan.
Loud noise. Silence others. Show respect. Forbid lies.
Hide fear. Show courage. Make flee. We fight as one Clan. Drive away Others.
Fell from sky. Killed many. Stone-beast’s skin. Shines as water. Cuts as stone.
Spear best for hunt. Spear best for fight. Spear best for fish. Spear just best.
Clan serves Mammoths. Mammoths serve The Clan. Together we are strong.
Hit far away. Hit well or chase. Better hit well. Chase make meat tough. Hate chase.
Tiger eats with it. Kill tiger. Now Clan can kill with it. And eat with it. Happy not smell like tiger mouth.
Furry big men. Fling arrows. Angry outsiders. Not start fight. Not let furry big men win.
Many days make net. Dire wolf hunts many moons. Days of work end moons of fear. Wolf hung in net is easy hit.
Skin tough. Tougher than spear. Knife can’t cut. Need crush. Crushing Rock Spear cracks Croc. Meat tender. Don’t overcook. Meat tough.
Three-legs, shining stone monster. Burns all near. Cannot fight. Can trick. Monster fall down. Make loud noise. Tastes like burning.
Steeped with herbs and essences from the deepest forest, when the sacred fumes rise up around me, truth and lie dissolve into revelation.
Given unto me as I did ascend to the priestly throne, when I donned this mask, the great jaguar’s power flowed through me as a river overflows its banks.
Quarried from the black earth in the House of Gloom, I decreed unto my followers that a great obsidian temple be raised to honor and appease the death god Ah Puch.
From whence came this strange skull? No mortal nor any god seems to know its source, but it whispers secrets when the moon is dark.
Ere I could wield spear or spell I honored the gods in the great ball courts of Ixkun.
The great serpent Ochan did speak unto me whilst I was but a babe in arms. It revealed the fearsome magicks that would save my people.
With great wrath, I cast curses upon the heads of mine enemies. All who threatened Ixkun feared my hexes.
This bird-like demon camest from the House of Gloom, and did set upon the innocent with its talons. I clipped its wings and speared its foul heart.
Impelled by visions, I sought the hidden threat amongst my people. A Nagual shapeshifter preyed upon our children until I struck this cursed crown from atop its head.
To touch the great serpent is to lay one’s hand upon the heart of time. I awoke with but one glorious feather, given unto me by Gukumatz.
As foretold in the great cosmic calendar, when the moon doth occult the sun, then this great ritual invocation of the Bacabs shall hearken a new age for my people.
With carven trifles, my descendents honor the great battles of yore. Some nights I project a vision of myself through these trinkets, and my people’ tormentors do quail and tremble.
I never understood fools who stand at ten paces waiting to be shot by some fop in a powdered wig. While he looked the other way, I plugged the baron’s barrel and naturally won the day.
The Terror took many heads in the Place de la Revolution. Even I could never be so cold and bloodthirsty as this marvel. It is, shall we say, and inspiration for me. We can always do more, no?
Even my cold heart can admire a flashy uniform and a finely-wrought sword. So of course I took poor Captain Dufort’s from him on the eve of Austerlitz. After our duel he had little need of it.
The young Tsar offered this amber-inlaid masterwork in payment for killing The Corsican. When Wellington beat me to it, I stole it for myself. I sadly learned later that Mother Russia never forgets.
I’ve no shame regarding my youthful banditry. The nobility had so much more than me, you see? But the fops could not even keep the wages for their hired guards from me.
My first night as a spy. Before the Paris mobs stormed it, I infiltrated the prison, overpowered the guards, and freed a certain depraved Marquis on behalf of a wealthy and perverted patron.
Count Cagliostro tasked me with planting a certain diamond necklace in The Queen’s chambers. I never dreamed the scandal might help launch a revolution.
Not his powdered wig. His wife’s wig. He wore it along with her plainest dress as a tried to escape The Terror. I caught him at the Italian border and he fought like a lion. A lion in a dress.
Citizen Robespierre charged me with ending this noble-coddling masked vigilante with a floral sobriquet. One of the great duels of my life, and the only foe even shiftier than I.
An ingenious explosive device, if it had gone off a few minutes sooner, the First Consul would have preceded me to the afterlife. Even so, it began in me a love affair with killer automatons.
A few changes to the master chef’s recipes and the addition of a hallucinogenic compound proved the distraction I needed to abscond with Prince Talleyrand’s private letters to the Emperor.
The petit corporal, he won so many battles. Some I even helped him win. But I saw his end coming before he did. These codes paid my way to safety across the English Channel.
Clan choked hills in gloom / Wintery discontent thrives / Mistaken past lies
Steeped water blooming / The kettle dictates the tea / Foes bones hold heat well
A forest for homes / Studied pruning through seasons / Bears bitterest cuts
Simple songs of old / A chord strung with dearest gut / Endings are never heard
Spinning steel flies through / Spring into summer passes / Youthful death bringer
First task and first sword / While duty done, Nobunga betrays / Blades without honor
Cracked crest in ashes / Oaths in honorable haste made / Vengeance on all
Honor lacks in void / Oni’s fury answers call / Demon, ninja, one
Dark smoke makes day night / Mitsuhide’s guise opens gates / Oni strength claims prize
Debts paid in shadow / What could demons want from us? / Four times four times, more
Treasured katana / Emperor knows shame and loss / Winter without Spring
Deeds done in darkness / Dancing lights, click, press, up, down / All time knows justice
I wore these proud arms in every battle since my youth, and hast won more titles, praises, and victories than any knight before or since.
My father named me for Charlemagne's greatest knight, and I ever endeavored to deserve the honor. Never did I read the book, for I speak not French. I am told ‘tis good.
For wont of this nail, I did lose mine horse. One thing led unto another and it did transpire the the whole kingdom was thus lost. T’was my squire’s fault.
Reduced to even a single card in a pasteboard game, my name lives on, symbol of triumphs past, with a Strength Rating of 100; twice hated Neville or despised Warwick’s meager 50.
From my youth as a squire until my first joust, I struck this wooden foe a thousand upon thousand times over so that my skill with lance knew no equal.
I lost but once in all my glorious days. I met Henry Percy on the lists and he unhorsed and near beheaded me, saved only by this piece of armor. Thus I swore unto the heavens to never lose again.
A golden trophy for a golden day, where I did face the best knights in the land in Battle Royale. We traded blows for many an hour, until but one brave and battered knight still stood.
A silken scarf of rosy scent, I wore it 'round my neck when I tilted with the Duke of York. I know not what grieved him more, losing by me or losing while I didst wear his wife’s favor.
Thinking me a knave and cur, those who didst conspire ‘gainst The King sought to enroll me in their ranks. T’was the last mistake they ever did make, and marked me well in King Henry’s eye.
His grace, King Henry commanded that I besiege Harfleur. I brooked no tiresome tunneling or cowardly waiting, but stormed the parapets and laid low the garrison with sword and valor.
Many a Frenchman did rue the day they faced Sir Roland at the Battle of Agincourt, while the King gave speeches about bands and brothers, I led the charge that set our the French foes to flight.

All England wept at my demise, including the young King Henry VI. Although he had known but two summers when I passed, I know in my breast that he didst weep for me and not his lost blankie as some do claim.
Every great idea I’ve had, I wrote down in this book the moment I had it. I used to have a book for the bad ideas too, but of course it never saw much use.
These ever so clever eyepieces let me gaze upon the world as the situation dictates. Be they microscopic, hyperchromatic, or pseudoetheric, all seeing needs are accounted for.
My dear aunties who raised me. I knew they’re proud, despite their old-fashioned prejudices against women scientists.

My time as Royal Engineer aboard the Air-Dreadnought Trafalgar was as thrilling as it was terrifying. I was sorry to leave her, but I did copied the Control Key, just in case I needed to borrow her some day.
As a stowaway, I had to prove myself to Captain Nemo lest he toss me overboard. This filter tripled the electro-field intensity and earned me a berth on the Nautilus.
This clever cog made my Bathyspheres roll at flank speed along the seafloor, so we could charge straight through the merfolk lines and smash their typhoon cannons to pieces.
A lady needs to take the airs from time to time. Also, how else was I supposed to board the Battle Balloons of Leng before they bombed Shanghai?
I designed this to settle a bar bet with my good friend Mr. Fogg, but it ended up proving vital in negotiating the Peace of Avalon in 1892.
Having captured Sir Sylvester Synister, we found no jail could hold him. So of course I simply invented a panoptical prison that confounded his every escape attempt.
When Nemo joined with the Atlantean Emperor to invade London, I was the first to stand against my old captain.
It took some doing to transform an Atlantean water weapon into something that could be used against Moleman Marauders beneath Paris.
Strictly speaking I did not invent it, but I did brew up a version that both kept its minty flavor for over an hour and can power an airship for a day when fed to an electric eel.
Prometheus himself dreams of stealing me magic match. I’ve lit a thousand beautiful bombs with this ever-fiery smolderin’ stick.
No scribbled chart nor wheezin’ wind ever set my course. I took to using old Rackham’s knucklebones in place of a magnet. Always had a nose for booty, did that hornswaggler.
A cyclone ne’er spun wilder than me ship’s wheel, but when she stopped as sure as saltpeter there be the enemy hindquarters, ripe for a broadside o’ cannonfire.
She’ll splinter yon hull with the power o’ Leviathan itself, a steel and sulfur ram’s head that were the scourge of all seven known and three unknown seas.
A loverly lucky coin with twice the heads of your other crowns. That be two more heads than what I left on the scallywag I won it off.
Stole this bit o’ manly marble from a certain Sultan. Now, it weren’t so crack’d and broke when me lads pulled it down, but he be a strapping fella all the same.
Sneaked this recipe from the King’s own alchemist, I did. The secret ingredient be vampire bat guano and ash from a burned orphanage.
Looted this rail from His Spanish Majesty’s own flagship. Shined like the devil’s horns when I fired me swivels from its golden perch.
Took this here curse’d coin from a skeleton’s hand. Me grenadoes took care of the rest of that boney undead band.
Swiped this precious parchment from Captain Mac, a crook’d and crazed Scotsman who drew this here map to his treasure trove in explosive ink.
Thieved this here loverly drink’n glass from a Javanese buccaneer. Fill with equal parts rum, gunpowder, and whale oil for a fine bit o’ fun.
Snatched from the head of the Atlantean Emperor his own self. T’was my miraculous water-proof powder that burst his throne room doors wide.
Can’t get outside without passing a Minder. I brain dumped the KindCorp Director of PR into my mirrorshades. Now everytime I think about food I’m full of doublespeak about the junk I feed my face.
No tech, no gizmos, just steel toes and rubber insulation. Did you know when you stomp the positronic brain of a GogDroid it gives off 20,000 volts? Wearing these, I didn’t need to know.

I know I sorta look like I fell face-first into a bowl of neon noodles. Milliseconds matter, so better to have superhuman reflexes from a little computer in your face than a lot of computer-targeted bullets in your heart.
I love this powered glove: Insulated against mal and hard warez. Custom knit to my hand. It’s so badass.

Taste of my youth! That’s how they get ya - put enough artificial everything into goop and it’ll taste like whatever. You’ll never notice the anger-dampening psychotropic additives. After I switched to bugs, I found my anger.
D-Corp Ceiling Drones kept us slummed. Get close and they tag and bag ya, then a long drop. I figured how to slip that twist and bagged the bot with his own sack. He dropped. I went up and out.

Sure the hair looks good. Hell, it looks great. But that’s pure bonus. Trick is, the nanodiamonds in the dye dazzle GogNet Mk 5 sensor arrays. Can’t lock on fast enough to stop me from blasting first.
We called ourselves the Right Wrong Cavaliers. We busted every D-Corp drone and hacked every GogNet node attached to the grid. These molten tungsten graffiti tags were our version of a calling card.

Nothing vital goes in a machine. You have a secret, you keep it analog. I had a lot of secrets. All the freakin’ secrets. Micro-engraved in coded tetrominos, no one outside of the Right Wrongs knew how to read ‘em.

Sweet piece of gear, disguised like a prop from a Bitsy the Clownbot costume. Activate within ten meters of a Quantum Drive and flip the Schrodinger State of every processor. Usually followed by a lot of smoke.
Shrinks down to the size of a pencil. Or at least I think so - never seen an actual pencil. Point is, it’s tiny, click, it’s big and has a very sharp point.

No matter where you go, there I am. This simulation called Valhalla might be heaven, but copies of my mind are back in the living world, making miniaturize mischief controlling self-replicating Ada action figs.

I had the original when I was a kid. It taught me everything I needed to know about being a hero: fight injustice, protect the powerless, and Never, Ever Kill. Those three rules became my mantra as a crime-fighter.
Looking to give my crime fighting a non-lethal extra punch, I made this from used electronics and metal bits out of broken appliances. KO’d myself testing it, but woke up before my manager saw me.

The climbing is actually the easy part. It’s the landing from six stories up that gets ya. Installed shock absorbers that ran all the way up to my knees. Worth it to see the fools chasing me gawk in disbelief.

When you publicly shame the city’s biggest fat cats and politicos by dropping an unconscious, criminal mayor on their dinner table, they generally issue a warrant for your arrest. I framed it and hung it on the wall.

The terror of my neighborhood hid behind his badge extorting protection money from my family’s bodega. I tricked him into confessing on video and made him wear his own cuffs when I turned him in to face justice.

Criminals mostly aren’t very bright. White collar crook or street-level enforcer, everyone’s scared of gadgets they don’t understand. This is just a box with two lights on it, but it’s gotten more confessions than the Pope.

This sinister syndicate of corrupt politicians and gun-running gangsters called themselves KABAL. I started stapling these patches to their shirts when I dropped off their unconscious asses at the FBI task force’s doorstep.
I find most of my leads on Twitter. Really. This phone uses military-grade encryption and doesn’t even make calls - just hijacks local wifi to access my Twitter account and collect anonymous tips.

Even I was surprised that the head of KABAL turned out to be The Mayor. His famous Emerald Four Leaf Clover tie pin didn’t bring him much luck the night I showed up at his inaugural ball to bring him to justice.

Three citizens caught my first fight with Master Zed on video, and some fourth dude edited them together with a soundtrack. My beatdown of Zed broke every YouTube record for both fights and music videos and made me world-famous.

When Zed teamed up with KABAL, they made him one monster of a gun. This shot-machine- sniper-flare-gun had something deadly for every poor fool who got in his way. I took a dozen bullets before I put the cuffs on him.

After I went down for good capturing Zed, my fame went up. Folks started tagging my face all over the city as a warning to the corrupt and evil. You see one of these, you’ll know justice is coming soon.
